sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** At 1,355 (~7.8x trailing, ~3.5% yield) DSNG is still cheap; Q1 growth plus B40 justify the recovery off the June low.
**Why wrong:** 7.8x is peak-earnings optics — at through-cycle CPO (~US$950-1,000) NAV is ~Rp566-1,320, below the 1,355 price (Appendix). Market pays for spot (~US$1,048) to persist; VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL pt6: supply arrives 2-4y after price peaks. Q1 is the decelerated base case (+17% NI vs +61% FY25), not a fresh trigger.
**What proves us wrong:** CPO holds ≥US$1,100 through FY2027 AND H1 FY2026 NI >+20% AND FY2025 AR gearing ≤0.35x — evidence the through-cycle price reset, not just elevated spot.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.markdown:
1. Two-buyer domestic concentration: 100% of CPO to Sinar Mas + Wilmar (AR2025 p.46) — bargaining-power risk.
2. OER give-back 23.92%→23.32% (AR2025 p.117) — unexplained efficiency slip.
3. Through-cycle NAV ~Rp566-1,320 < entry 1,355 even at B40-adjusted US$1,100 — the valuation kill is NOT resolved.
4. Land-revaluation BV inflation: pre-reval BV ~Rp888 vs reported ~Rp1,138 — P/B 1.19x reported ≈ 1.52x pre-reval.
5. Net-debt uncertainty: dossier ~42% gearing (≈Rp5T) vs T-001's 3.49T, flagged — higher figure bottoms the NAV band.
6. Board/commissioner overhaul at 9-Jun-2026 RUPST (T-001 Bear pt6) — unmodeled strategy/dividend risk.
7. EUDR (dossier "Key Risks"): certification cost + "potential exclusion from premium markets" overhang on the wood segment (~10% revenue, EU/US export) — uncaptured compliance/access risk.
